newsitem.title: GERMANY: German engineering wage talks start Monday.
newsitem.headline: German engineering wage talks start Monday.

text.p: The German IG Metall engineering trade union said Friday it was ready to make a start to 1997 wage negotiations on Monday as long as employers backed down on controversial plans to cut sick pay allowances.

Speaking after a four-hour meeting of its main board, IG Metall Chairman Klaus Zwickel said union negotiators had been given the go-ahead from regional union committees to hold national talks with the Gesamtmetall employers federation.
"We have confirmation that we can seek an overall deal through negotiations at the central level," Zwickel said.
Gesamtmetall separately issued a statement confirming that talks between the two were due to go ahead on Monday in a location on the outskirts of Frankfurt.

But Zwickel repeated that the union would accept no reductions in sick pay allowances, which employers are seeking to cut to 80 percent of salary from 100 percent in accordance with a new law that came into effect earlier this month.
"Sick payments must remain at 100 percent," Zwickel said.
Gesamtmetall said that it would be going into talks to secure a deal that did not burden employers with any new costs.
It did not, however, repeat earlier insistences for the cut in sick payments, which employers have estimated would cut around 12 billion marks ($7.8 billion) off German industry's labour costs.

The highly unusual move by the two sides to enter into wage talks before existing contracts come up for renewal at the end of the year has been triggered by worker protests earlier this month against attempts to reduce sick payments.
More than 100,000 workers at Daimler-Benz AG plants around the country laid down tools after the industrial giant attempted to put the new law into effect immediately.
Daimler and others were later forced to withdraw the sick pay cuts pending wider agreement with unions on a wage deal.
